I’m coming to see you (and some of you are coming to see me 🧺💛!)

One of my favorite parts of writing a book is getting the chance to meet the people who have welcomed me into their homes every day. 

This tour isn’t just about signing books it’s about sharing stories, answering your homemaking questions, giving hugs, and celebrating this wonderful community we’ve built together.
I’d be so honored if you joined me at one of these special events including a very special TOUR OF THE BASKET HOUSE🧺☺️

See if I’ll be in a city near you, and grab your tickets through the link in my bio (or visit geni.us/babsbooktour)

Available for pre-order today!! Homemaking with Babs will be on your doorstep September 1st! 

This book is truly the culmination of a lifetime of lessons, traditions, and practical homemaking wisdom, and I cannot wait to share it with you.

For years, you’ve been asking me to put everything I’ve learned about running a home into one place. Well...here it is.

This isn’t a coffee table book.  It’s a handbook. An owner’s manual. A workhorse of a book. 
The book you’ll reach for when you’re wondering:
Where do I even start?
How do I get organized?
How do I keep up without feeling overwhelmed?

Because the truth is... no one teaches us how to run a home.  Not all of us just naturally know how to care for a house, create routines, stay organized, or keep everything running smoothly. Most of us learn through trial and error, picking up little tips along the way.
I wanted to change that.

Inside, you’ll find the systems I’ve used for a lifetime.  From The Babs Method (just 15 minutes every morning and every evening) to simple daily, weekly, and monthly routines that help you stay ahead instead of constantly catching up.

Then we’ll walk through the year together.  Season by season.
🌷 Spring cleaning and decluttering
☀️ Summer outdoor living
🍂 Fall routines and family organization
❄️ Winter homemaking, hosting, and home care.
Plus seasonal checklists, organizing systems, DIY cleaners, home maintenance, and practical tips to help every room—and every season—feel a little easier.

My hope is that this becomes the book you pull off the shelf again and again whenever you need a little guidance, a little encouragement, or simply a better system.

Homemaking with Babs arrives September 1. Pre-order your copy today through the link in my bio!

and last but not least thank YOU for encouraging me to write it. 

XO,
Babs

Save this one for sports season and follow along for more life tested hacks

You can also find tips for everything life throws your way in my NEW  book Homemaking with Babs! Available now! 

Here’s the science: vodka contains ethanol, which kills the odor-causing bacteria responsible for that funky sports gear smell. And because alcohol evaporates quickly, the vodka smell disappears as it dries.

Just add plain, unflavored vodka to a spray bottle, lightly mist the gear, and let it air-dry completely.

Think pads, cleats, gloves, and other hard-to-wash gear that comes home smelling like… well, you know. 😅

Thank you to Stephanie Trotta @stephanietrotta , whose incredible sense of style touched every part of this book. From styling me and making everyone look their best to hand-selecting props and overall art direction, your impeccable eye shaped every page.

And as always, thank you to Alex Gill @alexgill , Desiree and Maria, whose special touch with hair and makeup made sure everyone looked and felt their very best throughout the shoot.

Thank you to Elisa Bulgrin of Longfield Farm @longfieldfarmct for the beautiful flowers and for helping bring our vision to life, and to Elsa Edmond for jumping right in.

To my Brunch with Babs team, Elizabeth my daughter, Laura Patterson, and Jill Ruscito. Your tireless work, care, and dedication made all of this possible.

And to Angelin Adams, Marysarah Quinn, thank you for making this book possible. To Cait Hoyt, Jordan Solomon and Abby Walters at CAA, thank you for believing in me and for your guidance.

I hoped Homemaking with Babs would be informative, useful, and beautiful. Seeing it at #1 makes everything that went into creating it even more special ❤️

From preschool teacher to New York Times bestselling author, Barbara Costello—better known as @brunchwithbabs—has built a following with her viral home hacks, entertaining tips, and approachable take on homemaking. 🩵 

At home in The Basket House, an 1830s Connecticut cottage that was once a basket shop, Babs brings that same warmth to a house layered with antiques, woven textures, and history.

Her latest book, Homemaking with Babs: Tips and Tricks for Making a House a Home, puts her signature approach to homemaking on the page.

If you have ever struggled to make your house truly feel like a home, you are not alone. That is why every seasonal chapter in Homemaking with Babs includes ideas for adding the comforting, personal touches that make a home feel like yours.

While we were in Charleston, we posted on Stories asking if anyone would let me come over and help organize their home.

Lauren invited us in.

We thought the day would be about sharing a few organizing tips, but what it became was so much more.

Lauren already had a beautiful, organized house. But since losing her mom two years ago shortly after she started building her house, she had been struggling to now make it truly feel like home. She missed having her mom there to say, “Okay, here is what you do.”

So we spent the day making small, comforting changes using ideas from my new book.

We brought her mother’s vase and silver out of storage. We displayed her children’s artwork, created a craft and homework cart for calmer afternoons, and framed old photographs of her mom so Lauren could see her every time she walked through the door.

Nothing we did completely changed her house. But each little detail made it feel warmer, more personal and more connected to the people she loves.

Because homemaking is not about having a perfect house or buying more things. It is about bringing the meaningful things you already have into your everyday life and creating a home where the people inside feel seen, loved and cared for.

Lauren later told me there were so many things she did not know she still needed her mom to teach her.

That is why I wrote Homemaking with Babs. So whenever you need a little motherly guidance, you can open the book and hear me say, “Okay, here is what you do.” ❤️

We celebrated Labor Day a little early this year because I was about to hit the road for the Homemaking with Babs book tour, and I couldn’t leave without squeezing in one last summer dinner at the beach❤️

And what a way to send off summer!

I did as much of the prep as I could at home, packed it all up, and finished dinner right at the beach. If your beach or park has grills available, take advantage of them! It’s such a fun way to turn an ordinary summer evening into something that feels really special. Just be sure to check your beach’s rules before you plan your menu.

Now that I’m home from the first stops of the book tour, I’m finally getting to share everything we made.

And what a menu it was!

What a week 💛 Homemaking with Babs is officially out in the world, and I don’t think I could have dreamed up a more special way to celebrate it. From sold-out events to early mornings, hundreds of hugs, a few flights, and so many unexpected moments along the way. 

We kicked things off on Sunday by opening the doors to the Basket House for the very first time and welcoming 60 of you inside. We signed books, toured the little 1800s home where so much of Homemaking with Babs came to life, and all of the proceeds from the event went to charity. It was the perfect place to begin with @elmstreetbooks 

On Monday, it was off to @bookendsnj  in New Jersey, where I got to meet so many wonderful people! 

Then we headed into NYC for a 4:30 AM wake up! I headed to @goodmorningamerica for not one, but TWO GMA segments celebrating Homemaking with Bas 

After GMA, it was over to @barnesandnoble on Fifth Avenue for another book signing. 

Next stop: Charleston! ✈️ 

The next morning, I did something I’ve never done before. I went to the home of one of you, someone I had never met in person before, and spent the day helping her make her house feel a little more like home. ❤️ It was such a special experience, and I’ll be sharing much more about that day very soon.

That evening we headed to @buxtonbooks_chs , where more than 300 of you came out to see us. And before I had even signed the first book, something pretty incredible happened.

The very first woman in line told me that she was a previous owner of the Basket House, and she had brought old photographs of the house with her! To start the tour by opening the doors to the Basket House in Connecticut and then meet someone connected to its history all the way down in Charleston felt like the most amazing full-circle moment.

To every single person who bought the book, came to an event, waited in line, shared a story, gave me a hug, or followed along from home, thank you from the bottom of my heart.

What a way to kick off the launch of  Homemaking with Babs 🫶 I’ll have my feet up all weekend reading @womansdaymag @womansworldmag

A special thank you to @birchlane for sponsoring such a special week.

The very first event of the Homemaking with Babs book tour felt especially meaningful because we held it right here at the Basket House. For the first time ever, we opened the doors and welcomed 60 of my online family inside to tour the home, hear some of its stories, and celebrate the book together.

The Basket House is where so much of Homemaking with Babs was photographed, so beginning the tour here felt like the perfect way to bring everything full circle.

And it reminded me of something I really wanted this book to capture: homemaking is about so much more than cleaning and organizing.

Yes, it is about creating systems that make life easier, staying on top of home maintenance, building routines that work, and having seasonal checklists and practical tips to help you care for your home.

But it is also about what happens inside that home.

It is about gathering around the table, welcoming people in, feeding the people you love, celebrating together, and making your home a place people want to return to.

That is why Homemaking with Babs also includes so much of what I have learned over a lifetime of hosting and entertaining, from how to set a table and the entertaining essentials I always keep on hand, to simple ways to spruce up for the season and even my trick for nearly doubling the size of your table when you need a few more seats.

Because your home is meant to be cared for, but it is also meant to be lived in, gathered in, and shared.

What a special way to begin this book tour and thank you @birchlane for helping make this such a special day! 

Homemaking with Babs is available tomorrow

We aren’t born knowing how to run a home, and they certainly don’t teach us in school.

After more than 50 years of homemaking, I wanted to put everything I’ve learned in one place. The things your mother taught you, the things she may have forgotten to teach you, and the things you usually only learn after years of figuring them out yourself.

Homemaking with Babs is filled with my tried-and-true DIY cleaners, cleaning routines, seasonal schedules, home maintenance checklists, organizing systems, and all those little tips that make taking care of a home so much easier.

Whether you’re moving into your very first home or you’ve been taking care of one for decades, I hope this is the book you keep nearby, turn to when you need it, and eventually pass along to someone you love.

It’s the owner’s manual your home should have come with. 🤍

Homemaking with Babs arrives September 1!

What if just 15 minutes in the morning and 15 minutes at night could change more than your home?

The Babs Method is just one of the practical, life-changing systems inside Homemaking with Babs. I poured a lifetime of knowledge into this book to help your home run more smoothly—and help you feel calmer and more in control.

When everything around you is piling up, your mind carries the weight of every unfinished task. You can feel behind before the day has even begun.

But a few simple routines can change that. Your home stays manageable, your mind feels clearer, and you stop using so much energy worrying about everything you still need to do.

It isn’t about having a perfect home. It’s about creating simple systems that give you more peace, more energy, and more time for the life happening inside it.

When your home feels lighter, your mind does too. 🤍
